comparison: Same Hackathon and lifecycle states across three levels of expression

prompts.prompt:
Create a high fidelity website UI concept board for HackJudge, a technical competition platform. Wide landscape board, TWO equal-size desktop homepage designs side by side: left "Before the event · Zero projects", right "During the event · First submissions". At top small caption "Visual exploration · Sample event details". It must be actual flat web interface design with readable content, no devices, no photography of a screen, no poster-only art. Both views use same example event "CivicHacks 2026", October 12, Innovation Center. Shared top navigation HackJudge / Events / Sign in. This homepage automatically leads with next event, secondary all events link at bottom. BEFORE EVENT NO project names, no team names, no images, no fake project counts, prize/attendance claims. Before contents: event purpose "Build practical tools for stronger communities.", View event and How to participate actions, a substantial three-track challenge area with Energy & climate / Access & inclusion / Public life and short meaningful descriptions, build timeline 09:00 Kickoff / 10:00 Build / 15:00 Submit / 16:00 Demo, judging criteria Innovation / Impact / Execution. DURING EVENT same identity, event phase Building is underway, timeline highlights Build, shows deadline 15:00 and exactly two minimally populated project rows: Voltify / Community energy-demand forecasting / Energy & climate, AgriSense / Field sensors and crop insights / Public life. No screenshots, logos, team names or invented repositories. Text "Judging opens after submissions close". Projects arriving are integrated modestly, never a huge empty gallery. Secondary calendar near bottom with Community showcase / Oct 25 and Code & Tell / Nov 9, All events link. Maintain functionality and readable familiar buttons. Theme must remain cohesive across both views. The user likes the content hierarchy and is now exploring layout, background, color scheme and typography. This board has two states of ONE creative direction, not two unrelated designs. No sci-fi neon, no biotech green, no generic SaaS template.
CREATIVE LEVEL 1: restrained but crafted. Board title "01 / Clear cut". Direction is a crisp competition program grounded in precise typography and a useful quiet interface. COOL PALE BLUE-GRAY canvas #E9EFF3, near-white working sections, deep navy text #142839, deep petrol BLUE accent #005B83 with white action labels. NOT cobalt on blank white. TYPOGRAPHY: humanist sans body and a broad medium-heavy grotesk heading, slightly rounded but mature, normal widths and less condensed than earlier concept. Event title 44px, clear size hierarchy. LAYOUT: generous full-width horizontal event masthead instead of split hero, title left and date/location/actions grouped right. Below 60% challenges arranged as editorial rows with headings and concise prose, 40% 'Your build day' vertical chronological agenda on a dark blue flat rectangular region. Judging criteria are a quiet horizontal three-column plain footer row. During state same masthead, challenge rows contract into a compact horizontal strip, two arriving project rows become main left section while agenda persists right. Clean thin blue-gray rules and thoughtful whitespace, small 5px control corners, no heavy shadows. Design value is composition, proportion and carefully balanced color. It should feel familiar and easy to operate without looking like a templated dashboard.

CREATIVE LEVEL 2: distinctive and energetic, carefully art-directed competition BUILD SHEET. Board title "02 / Build sheet". PALETTE: WARM LIGHT YELLOW paper background #FFF3CA, charcoal ink #25251F, strong BURNT VERMILION #B73716 accents and action fills with white labels, occasional pale ivory inset #FFFBEB. No gradient, no texture or fake grain. TYPOGRAPHY: bold tall condensed industrial sans for event title and challenge headings, title 64px, clear normal sans for body and functional labels, tabular timetable numerals. LAYOUT: header a narrow ink bar with light wordmark and nav, event title takes left 42% and spans two lines CIVICHACKS / 2026 with normal readable case if better. A compact date/location column sits immediately beside title, avoiding conventional marketing hero. Three large challenge tracks take right 58% as staggered flush rectangular text bands, colored cream/ink/vermilion carefully with readable type, each band has actual track heading and one useful short sentence; NO icon cards, no fake control knobs. A bold full-width timeline running horizontally across middle is an actual event itinerary, with connecting thin rule and strong times. Lower clean rubric strip plus secondary calendar. During: event title keeps its scale, right area becomes two project rows in pale ivory with compact track labels; challenge names remain in a compact strip above; build phase marked in vermilion timetable. Strong ink dividing rules, restrained 2px control corners, no offset shadows, no torn paper. At a glance this feels like a well-designed makers' competition program, bolder than conventional SaaS but entirely legible and operational.

CREATIVE LEVEL 3: boldly themed COMPETITION BROADCAST, drawing on live sports broadcast schedules and contemporary creative technology event graphics, translated into a usable builder platform. Board title "03 / Competition broadcast". PALETTE: deep PLUM canvas #2B153E and panels #39234D, warm off-white type #FFF9EA, lively GOLDEN YELLOW #F8D34F primary actions with deep plum labels, local saturated CORAL #F08A74 and pale lavender sections as deliberate large color blocks, never neon glow or gradients. TYPOGRAPHY: exaggerated heavy wide grotesk event title, 64px and tight but readable, compact clear sans controls/body. No mono cosplay. LAYOUT: main homepage looks like a striking broadcast event slate: narrow light navigation band, large title CIVICHACKS 2026 occupying an asymmetric left half, date/location and primary action directly underneath. Right side full-height stacked three-track challenge board, gold band for Energy & climate, pale lavender band for Access & inclusion, coral band for Public life, each track band includes useful prose in dark plum and a distinct geometric arrangement but no decorative abstract covers. Below a full-width light schedule rail looks like program guide with four chronological columns; current phase uses gold highlight. A compact offwhite lower section explains criteria and next calendar events. During: same plum event identity left, event live/building status is clear, right challenge bands compress into a horizontal mini-rail and two arriving projects appear as substantial light text rows with names and concise descriptions. Keep functional buttons conventional and clear, no trophy/leaderboard/ranks, no gamification, no arcade controls, no scoreboard counts. Theme is bold graphic composition at page scale while content and actions remain mature. Absolutely no invented project media before or during. Wildness comes from scale, color-field arrangement and lettering, not meaningless ornament.
